bangkok/creative-renaissance-video.keyIdea: Bangkok creatives restore older buildings and mix traditional culture with new art rather than replacing everything.
bangkok/creative-renaissance-video.tradeoff: Making art welcoming takes work beyond simply saving an old building.
bangkok/creative-renaissance-video.designUse: Turn restored buildings into welcoming places for local creative work.

bangkok/food-identity-video.keyIdea: Bangkok's independent food shops help give the city a character that chain restaurants cannot easily replace.
bangkok/food-identity-video.tradeoff: Independent shops are disappearing, putting their distinctive food and local character at risk.
bangkok/food-identity-video.designUse: Reserve affordable space for independent cooks alongside larger food businesses.

bangkok/river-boats-video.keyIdea: At Sathorn Pier, Bangkok's boats connect river trips with trains, nearby hotels, and places to visit.
bangkok/river-boats-video.tradeoff: Different counters, flags, and waiting areas can make choosing the right boat confusing.
bangkok/river-boats-video.designUse: Match signs at shared stops to each service and waiting area.

bangkok/songkran-city-ritual.keyIdea: Bangkok's Songkran brings family and temple customs into streets shared by local people and visitors.
bangkok/songkran-city-ritual.tradeoff: A water-party image can hide the festival's family ties and deeper meanings.
bangkok/songkran-city-ritual.designUse: Explain a celebration's meaning alongside rules for sharing crowded streets.

bangkok/green-escape.keyIdea: Bangkok's Benjakitti Park turns former industrial land into green public space with water, walking routes, and shade.
bangkok/green-escape.tradeoff: Parks need valuable land and upkeep, reducing space available for short-term profit.
bangkok/green-escape.designUse: Keep useful land for free green spaces that manage heat and water.

bangkok/city-of-design.keyIdea: Bangkok treats design as a way to improve everyday streets, shops, and public spaces, not just luxury products.
bangkok/city-of-design.tradeoff: Beautiful or efficient designs may still create difficulties for other users.
bangkok/city-of-design.designUse: Ask ordinary users how redesigned spaces could make daily tasks easier.

tokyo/metro-economics-video.keyIdea: Tokyo connects commuter trains directly with subway tracks, reducing transfers, while shared payment cards simplify journeys.
tokyo/metro-economics-video.tradeoff: Distance-based fares mean people making longer journeys must pay more.
tokyo/metro-economics-video.designUse: Join rail routes and payment systems so passengers change less often.

tokyo/vending-machines-video.keyIdea: Tokyo's vending machines provide goods around the clock, and some reuse cooling heat to warm drinks.
tokyo/vending-machines-video.tradeoff: Operators still refill machines, while convenience stores compete for customers and locations.
tokyo/vending-machines-video.designUse: Reuse waste heat inside equipment that offers services throughout the day.

tokyo/urban-history-video.keyIdea: Tokyo's rebuilding after fires and earthquakes changed street layouts and expanded railways into new residential areas.
tokyo/urban-history-video.tradeoff: The changes followed disasters that destroyed homes and large parts of the city.
tokyo/urban-history-video.designUse: Use rebuilding plans to connect new homes with safe transport routes.

tokyo/earthquake-readiness.keyIdea: Tokyo protects emergency roads by strengthening nearby buildings, linking city rescue plans with everyday household preparation.
tokyo/earthquake-readiness.tradeoff: Dense housing, damaged services, and stranded commuters can still make disaster response difficult.
tokyo/earthquake-readiness.designUse: Protect rescue routes while helping households plan supplies and communication.

tokyo/harajuku-fashion.keyIdea: In Harajuku, young people mix different clothes and styles to show who they are in public.
tokyo/harajuku-fashion.tradeoff: Tourism and big brands can turn many personal styles into one simple image.
tokyo/harajuku-fashion.designUse: Leave public space for young people to display their own styles.

tokyo/sento-neighborhoods.keyIdea: Tokyo's public bathhouses now offer shared local spaces, as more people have bathrooms in their own homes.
tokyo/sento-neighborhoods.tradeoff: Bathhouses cannot depend only on washing services when people can wash at home.
tokyo/sento-neighborhoods.designUse: Give older shared facilities new uses while keeping familiar local routines.

seoul/subway-system-video.keyIdea: Seoul's subway uses platform doors and camera inspections to improve safety, while stations also host shops and performances.
seoul/subway-system-video.tradeoff: Safety equipment alone cannot replace ongoing cleaning, inspection, and customer service.
seoul/subway-system-video.designUse: Combine transport safety features with regular checks and welcoming station spaces.

seoul/gyeongbokgung-video.keyIdea: Seoul's Gyeongbokgung combines palace buildings, a guard ceremony, and museum displays to share parts of Korean history.
seoul/gyeongbokgung-video.tradeoff: A short ceremony can show only one part of the palace's past.
seoul/gyeongbokgung-video.designUse: Pair live demonstrations with displays that explain the history behind them.

seoul/korea-history-video.keyIdea: Moving the royal capital to Seoul made the city part of a wider change in Korea's government.
seoul/korea-history-video.tradeoff: A change of capital shifts political activity away from the previous center.
seoul/korea-history-video.designUse: Show how changes in government move important places within a region.

seoul/hallyu-wave.keyIdea: Seoul's entertainment businesses spread Korean culture through training, online sharing, translation, and fans who introduce it to others.
seoul/hallyu-wave.tradeoff: Workers can become vulnerable when demand or technology changes quickly.
seoul/hallyu-wave.designUse: Help audiences discover local culture through translations and active fan communities.

seoul/cheonggyecheon-restoration.keyIdea: Seoul removed road infrastructure to uncover Cheonggyecheon, bringing water and pedestrian space back into the city center.
seoul/cheonggyecheon-restoration.tradeoff: Removing roads can affect drivers, nearby shops, and the public budget.
seoul/cheonggyecheon-restoration.designUse: Replace selected traffic spaces with water routes where people can walk and rest.

seoul/bukchon-hanok.keyIdea: In Bukchon, visiting hours and clear signs help tourists share old streets with people who live there.
seoul/bukchon-hanok.tradeoff: The same narrow streets that attract visitors also bring noise and privacy problems.
seoul/bukchon-hanok.designUse: Guide visitors through heritage areas without disrupting residents' homes and routines.

singapore/urban-design-video.keyIdea: Singapore's public housing puts schools, shops, parks, and transport near homes, making many daily needs easier to reach.
singapore/urban-design-video.tradeoff: Residents receive long leases, but the state still owns the apartments.
singapore/urban-design-video.designUse: Place everyday services near homes and connect them to public transport.

singapore/hawker-culture-video.keyIdea: Singapore's hawker centers bring different food traditions together, with regular customers returning for particular cooks and dishes.
singapore/hawker-culture-video.tradeoff: Hard work and competition can discourage younger people from taking over stalls.
singapore/hawker-culture-video.designUse: Support new cooks in learning dishes from experienced local stallholders.

singapore/changi-jewel-video.keyIdea: Singapore's Jewel airport complex opens indoor gardens to residents as well as travelers, without requiring a flight ticket.
singapore/changi-jewel-video.tradeoff: Crowds can make even short walks through the gardens take longer.
singapore/changi-jewel-video.designUse: Open attractive transport spaces to nearby residents as well as passengers.

singapore/water-security.keyIdea: Singapore uses several water sources, including cleaned used water, to reduce dependence on any single supply.
singapore/water-security.tradeoff: Desalination needs energy and infrastructure, while local water collection requires protected land.
singapore/water-security.designUse: Combine different water supplies and protect the places that collect rain.

singapore/language-policy.keyIdea: Singapore uses English across communities while teaching home languages to keep cultural identity and family connections.
singapore/language-policy.tradeoff: A common working language can weaken home languages and the memories they carry.
singapore/language-policy.designUse: Use a shared service language while keeping room for home languages.

singapore/gardens-by-the-bay.keyIdea: Singapore's Gardens by the Bay brings plants, buildings, and paths together to help visitors notice nature.
singapore/gardens-by-the-bay.tradeoff: Lights, tourist photos, and paid areas can make the garden feel artificial.
singapore/gardens-by-the-bay.designUse: Build green visitor spaces that show different plants and explain their needs.

paris/city-history-video.keyIdea: Paris replaced many medieval streets with wide boulevards, changing how the city looked as it grew.
paris/city-history-video.tradeoff: New roads removed parts of the older street pattern and buildings.
paris/city-history-video.designUse: Explain which older features a street rebuilding project would replace.

paris/cafe-culture-video.keyIdea: Paris cafes give regular customers a place to meet and watch street life beyond their small homes.
paris/cafe-culture-video.tradeoff: Visitors expecting quick service may find the relaxed pace frustrating.
paris/cafe-culture-video.designUse: Make places to sit socially without rushing people through their visit.

paris/louvre-history-video.keyIdea: The Louvre changed from a fortress into a royal home and then a museum, reflecting changing public roles.
paris/louvre-history-video.tradeoff: Reusing the building involved repeated extensions and construction across many generations.
paris/louvre-history-video.designUse: Adapt important buildings for new public roles while showing earlier uses.

paris/seine-world-heritage.keyIdea: The Seine's banks link bridges, old buildings, and walking routes, showing how Paris grew beside the river.
paris/seine-world-heritage.tradeoff: Choosing which places to preserve can leave some groups' stories less visible.
paris/seine-world-heritage.designUse: Connect riverside paths with signs explaining different layers of local history.

paris/cycling-city.keyIdea: Paris adds bike lanes, slower streets, and pedestrian areas to make short journeys easier without a car.
paris/cycling-city.tradeoff: Quieter streets can help residents but inconvenience drivers and delivery workers.
paris/cycling-city.designUse: Balance safer short journeys with practical access for deliveries and businesses.

paris/tourism-pressure.keyIdea: Paris tourism supports jobs and cultural places, but crowds and visitor expectations also disrupt ordinary city life.
paris/tourism-pressure.tradeoff: Crowds and short-term rentals can make neighborhoods harder for residents to live in.
paris/tourism-pressure.designUse: Plan visitor routes around the everyday needs of people living nearby.
